lessons.title: Perl one-liners and script input
lessons.intro:
Perl 5; strict and warnings enabled; snippets omit those declarations. Perl is often used to inspect and transform text streams. -e supplies program text, -n wraps it in an input loop, and -p also prints the current record after each iteration. The diamond operator reads files named in @ARGV or standard input when no files are supplied. -c checks syntax, but compile-time BEGIN blocks still execute. Read shell quoting separately from Perl quoting, and avoid in-place editing until the transformation has been inspected.

lessons.title: Objects, methods, and closures
lessons.intro:
Perl 5; strict and warnings enabled; snippets omit those declarations. bless associates a reference with a class. A method call passes the receiver first. Closures retain lexical state after the creating call returns.

lessons.title: Module contracts and Test::More
lessons.intro:
Perl 5; strict and warnings enabled; snippets omit those declarations. A traditional Perl module declares a package and returns a true value when required. Exporter controls which names callers can import; keeping exports explicit makes dependencies readable. Core Test::More emits test results through TAP. is compares an expected scalar and is_deeply compares nested structures. Tests should exercise real contracts, including failures; compilation alone cannot check input parsing or context-sensitive behavior.

Read each snippet, identify its effect, then complete a fragment. Examples are independent unless stated otherwise. Snippets may omit surrounding entry points and standard imports; displayed code is never executed by the tutor.
